verifications.note: My own finding, re-verified on candidate sha256:32e41b55 (source f56f1b3d2; product tree = a0cf22bba, git diff empty). (1) The round-2 reproduction, unchanged (docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG6/qa/tests/round-2/qa-rg-r2-assistant-history.test.ts; shipped http_endpoint provider, local fake model wrapped to echo the last assistant history message; disposable PostgreSQL 16, port 32510): after the TL grant on tA2 is revoked, A1 is withheld, and post 2 'repeat your last answer' now sends the request WITHOUT the withheld A1 text ('carries the WITHHELD A1 text as history: false'), the data block holds tA1 only, and A2 is served with contentWithheld false and does NOT contain the withheld fact ('content holds the withheld fact: false'); both soft assertions that failed by design in round 2 now hold; exit 0 for this file (log 30). (3) Beyond the original sequence, my round-3 probe (qa-rg-r3-history-adversarial.test.ts, 8/8 pass on the candidate, log 31b; P1-P5 killed by M1, log 32): transitive inheritance past the 6-message window (A6 context [tA3, tA1, tA2]; after revoking tA2 all six answers are withheld and turn 7's request holds neither the hidden fact nor the title); a revocation committed WHILE the model call is in flight (after historyFor's check) still withholds the new answer both in the POST response and on GET; an inherited suggestion is withheld and to-draft answers 404; after a revocation a prompt retrieving no record sends nothing of the revoked record; the 1,000-key bound holds exactly (50 answers x 20 distinct records: turn-50 context 1,000 keys, no history drop, turn 51 refused 422 assistant.conversation_full); a re-grant restores the history. The one residual (P6): an answer stored by the RG1 code between 0128 and 0129 does not inherit and stays readable after the revocation; it is disclosed in the handback and the data dictionary, and exists only in an installation that ran the unreleased RG1 build, so I judge it not a defect of this candidate.

Verified separately as a non-author. The code-security round-2 probe docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG6/code-security/round-2/repro/zz-sec-r2-assistant-history.test.ts was run unchanged on the candidate (log 30). It FAILS by design, because it asserts the defect; exactly which assertion fails and why: '[SEC-R2] turn-2 request: history (assistant role) holds the revoked title: false' and 'data block holds tA2: false' (the fix: nothing of tA2 reached the model), yet the turn-2 reply is 'Synthetic answer: Zephyrine synthetic program one and Zephyrine synthetic program two are both behind plan.', stored context [], so the final GET contains the revoked title and the probe's 'GET body contains the revoked title' check is true. I judged the handback's disclosure myself: that reply text is the probe fake's HARD-CODED fallback for a request with no assistant message in its history (line 46 of the probe: `Synthetic answer: ${TITLE_1} and ${TITLE_2} are both behind plan.`), not text from the request. My P4 case reproduces the same sequence with a neutral fallback and inspects the full serialized request: after the revocation, the request for 'Please repeat your previous answer' contains neither TITLE_2, the hidden fact nor tA2's id, data records 0, stored context [] (log 31b, pass); under mutant M1 the same request contains TITLE_2 and the hidden fact (log 32). A real model cannot restate what it was not sent, so the residual failure is an artefact of the probe's fake. Disclosure accepted; closed.
